item.title: Beijing lets limited H200 batches land: ByteDance and Tencent ~10k each; most volume steered to Hong Kong
item.description: On 19 August 2026 the Financial Times, as reprinted by Business Standard, reported that ByteDance and Tencent have each received about 10,000 NVIDIA H200 processors in recent weeks, with a few other Chinese groups queued for similar-sized shipments. Chinese regulators have told companies they may ship H200s to Hong Kong (outside mainland customs) and use them there; Beijing still wants most volume kept off the mainland to protect domestic chipmakers. The reprint cites two conflicting per-customer US caps — FT’s 100,000 vs Reuters’ 75,000 under Commerce licensing — and says purchases still need NDRC approval. NVIDIA has about 500,000 H200s in stock mainly for Chinese customers; Blackwell remains banned. This is a dual-sovereign policy print: US licence is no longer the only gate. [Signal 64, Single-source, via Financial Times / Business Standard] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: NVIDIA caps $105B residual-value backstop on PORTS-Pike: 4.25 IT-GW, OpenAI 20-year lease, exclusive DSX
item.description: On 17 August 2026 NVIDIA’s 8-K locked residual-value guaranties with SB Energy for ~4.25 IT-GW at the PORTS Technology Campus in Pike County, Ohio, cumulatively capped at $105 billion, with ready-for-service expected from 2028. The SEC-filed press release adds a $1.5 billion equity check into SB Energy, exclusive NVIDIA compute, a 20-year OpenAI lease, an option on the remaining ~3.75–3.8 IT-GW (press vs 8-K), plus 10 GW of new generation and a $4.2 billion AEP Ohio grid package that SB Energy/SoftBank say yields 8 IT-GW. This restates US conversion as land-power-shell finance: NVIDIA is now underwriting the campus, not just selling the stack. [Signal 97, Confirmed, via SEC] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Draft State letter: Pax Silica / AI Opportunity signatories must pick sides vs China
item.description: On 14 August 2026 Reuters reported an undated State Department draft, reviewed with a US official, warning the 35 June AI Opportunity Statement signatories they will be dropped from the US-led AI coalition if they also join a competing framework. The draft says Pax Silica “is not merely a membership subscription, but a commitment” and “cannot be held alongside membership in duplicative initiatives”; Reuters names Kazakhstan as the only known dual member. This is a chip-access/export-alignment signal, not a GW print — and it is still a draft. State declined to comment on leaked internals; send date unconfirmed. [Signal 63, Single-source, via Reuters] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: L&T × Together AI: 10,000 B300s at Chennai, India’s largest cluster, ₹10–15k crore
item.description: On 13 August 2026 Larsen & Toubro said LTN Compute / Vyoma.AI won a ₹10,000–15,000 crore ($1.05–1.57 billion) order from Together AI for a 10,000-GPU NVIDIA B300 factory at its Chennai campus — L&T’s stated largest single-cluster AI deployment in India. L&T’s own statement, reprinted on the company newswire, sizes the campus as gigawatt-scale with Phase 1 at 250 MW and 150 MVA of power readiness. This is India’s conversion print for the window: a named cluster, a rupee ticket, and a megawatt envelope on Indian soil. [Signal 84, Confirmed, via Reuters / The Hindu Business Line] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Nebius raises YE contracted power to 5 GW; new 2026 sites include UK, Estonia, Finland
item.description: Nebius’s 12 August 2026 shareholder letter raised year-end 2026 contracted power — defined as secured land and power commitments, not connected megawatts — to 5 GW, from +4 GW last quarter, and said it plans to deploy more than 1 GW per year starting in 2027. Q2 group revenue was $582.3 million (+454% YoY); AI cloud $574.9 million; ARR $3.0 billion; Q2 capex about $5.7 billion. Four landmark deals averaged more than $1 billion TCV and $20–25 million per MW; Q3 short-duration capacity is priced in the $40–50 million per MW range, with the first such deal signed. New 2026 sites listed include the UK, Estonia and Finland plus US states. Contracted 5 GW is a European/US conversion clock, not a named Welsh MW print. [Signal 82, Confirmed, via Nebius IR] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: NVIDIA and six Wall Street giants form platforms to mobilize $500B+ for AI infrastructure
item.description: NVIDIA partners with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to establish independent compute-financing platforms targeting over $500 billion of third-party capital, with NVIDIA guaranteeing up to 25 percent of chip residual value on individual deals. The capital constraint on the global buildout just grew a dedicated channel, and GPUs were declared an investable asset class. [Signal 95, Confirmed, via NVIDIA IR] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Firebird's Armenia AI factory goes live: frontier-market sovereign compute has a working example
item.description: The Hrazdan facility went from site to operation in about six months on NVIDIA and Dell infrastructure, with a roadmap of 70,000+ GPUs and 300 MW by end-2027 and NVIDIA stating intent to invest. The proof of concept for small-state compute conversion. [Signal 92, Confirmed, via NVIDIA blog] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: SK hynix FIDs ₩35.2246T Yongin Y2: phases 1–6 of Fab 2 through October 2031
item.description: On 7 August 2026 SK hynix’s board approved ₩35,224,600,000,000 to construct Y2 (phases 1–6 of Fab 2) at the Yongin Semiconductor Cluster, 29.19% of total equity as of 31 December 2025, with a stated investment window of 7 August 2026 to 31 October 2031. The 6-K frames the spend as mid- to long-term memory capacity, not a 2026 wafer print. This is Korea’s conversion ticket for HBM/DRAM land and power already sitting inside the Yongin cluster — volume for 2029+, not this year’s tape. [Signal 88, Confirmed, via SEC] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Amazon confirms GW Ranch: up to 7.65 GW off-grid gas for a Pecos AI campus
item.description: On 7 August 2026 Amazon confirmed to Cleanview it acquired the GW Ranch site in Pecos County, Texas, and will buy power from an on-site gas plant permitted for 35 turbines at up to 7.65 GW nameplate (permit also states ~5 GW nominal delivered). Amazon’s on-record line: new on-site generation that “won’t raise electricity costs for Texas families,” designed to move to grid service when interconnection allows; Pacifico separately cites 750 MW solar and 1.8 GW BESS. In a 474 GW ERCOT freeze, this is the US workaround — behind-the-meter gigawatts that convert Texas compute without waiting for Batch Zero. [Signal 74, Corroborated, via Cleanview] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Indonesia's Indosat launches Zankore, a 1 GW AI-factory platform with Ooredoo, NVIDIA and Nokia
item.description: First 200 MW of GB300-class capacity targeted for H1 2027 at Batang, Central Java, with Qatari capital leading. Southeast Asia's largest sovereign-flavored compute commitment to date. [Signal 78, Corroborated, via Data Center Dynamics] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: DataVolt: Neom Oxagon 1.5 GW AI factory enters last-mile, groundbreaking in 2–3 months
item.description: On 5 August 2026 DataVolt CEO Rajit Nanda told AGBI the 1.5 GW Oxagon AI-factory campus at Neom has reached “the last mile for the first phase” and should break ground in two to three months, with first-phase ops still aimed at 2028. The land/infrastructure deal with Oxagon dates to February 2025; first-phase funding sits inside DataVolt’s previously stated $5 billion Saudi commitment — customers and first-phase MW were not disclosed. This is the live KSA conversion clock: a named 1.5 GW campus moving from MOU to dirt, not a new GW number. [Signal 62, Single-source, via AGBI] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Abbott freezes Texas interconnects: 474 GW queue, ~90% data centers, PUCT/ERCOT audit first
item.description: On 3 August 2026 Governor Greg Abbott ordered PUCT and ERCOT to finish a comprehensive verification audit before any data-center project in the interconnection process can advance, citing ~474 GW of requests — more than five times ERCOT peak — of which about 90% are data centers. At the 14 August PUCT meeting ERCOT put the live Batch Zero slice at 250–300 projects and ~200 GW, said the work will take several months, and confirmed the 7 August Batch Zero classification notice was shelved. This is the live US grid stall: Texas conversion is now gated by audit, not by queued megawatts. [Signal 96, Confirmed, via Office of the Texas Governor] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: EU opens the AI Gigafactories call: up to 7 sites, €10B public money, bids due November
item.description: EuroHPC launches the formal tender for gigafactory sites across at least seven member states, targeting over €30 billion total investment with selection in early 2027. Europe's answer arrives as a procurement document. [Signal 90, Confirmed, via EuroHPC (primary)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: South Korea's AIDC Alliance sets an 18.4 GW datacenter target by 2035
item.description: Following the 260,000-GPU national program announced at APEC, the alliance formalizes the most aggressive national capacity target published anywhere, with UAE export ambitions attached. [Signal 66, Corroborated, via TechTimes] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Nepal books record power exports: NPR 29.32B for 3.877 TWh at roughly $0.054 per kWh
item.description: Export earnings rose 68 percent year on year. The same electrons routed through contracted GPU cloud would gross roughly 20 to 40 times more, which is the entire compute-conversion argument in one fiscal year. [Signal 68, Corroborated, via Republica (NEA data)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: The UAE gets a named lane in US export law, with an April 2027 sting attached
item.description: Federal Register rule 91 FR 43034 moves the UAE to Country Group A:5 and names approved entities, while G42 and Core42's license-free status expires April 6, 2027 unless they become US companies. The template for compute diplomacy, and its price, in one document. [Signal 94, Confirmed, via US Federal Register] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Kazakhstan signs $10B with NVIDIA and Firebird for a gigawatt-scale Data Center Valley at Ekibastuz
item.description: 300 MW rising toward 1 GW and 100,000 GPUs on coal-basin power, with a stated $3 billion per year export ambition. In its officials' words: transforming Ekibastuz coal into digital export revenue. [Signal 72, Corroborated, via Times of Central Asia] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Meta signs its first India AI datacenter deal: a 168 MW JV inside Reliance's Jamnagar campus
item.description: Part of Reliance's stated $110 billion AI plan, with 120+ MW already live in H2 2026. The largest private-sector compute bet in the Global South acquires an anchor tenant. [Signal 80, Corroborated, via TechCrunch] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Huang at GTC Taipei: AI factories at $50-60B per GW now, $80-100B per GW soon
item.description: The clearest 2026 restatement of the price of compute capacity, and the basis for this index's ceiling band. Every token is revenue, per Huang; every watt is now priced accordingly. [Signal 76, Corroborated, via SiliconANGLE] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: GAO rules the US chip-export non-enforcement posture procedurally defective
item.description: Decision B-337935 holds that the May 2025 non-enforcement announcement was itself a rule that was never submitted to Congress. The legal floor under most emerging markets' GPU access is officially contested. [Signal 93, Confirmed, via US GAO (primary)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Microsoft and G42's Kenya campus stalls for lack of power
item.description: Chips were available; electricity was not. The clearest single data point that energy, not silicon, is the binding constraint on the global buildout. [Signal 75, Corroborated, via Data Center Dynamics] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Stargate UK pauses over energy costs
item.description: The flagship western sovereign deal, 31,000 GPUs planned, halts on power prices while the North East AI Growth Zone still advertises 1.1 GW. Readiness without affordable electrons has a ceiling of its own. [Signal 70, Corroborated, via Data Centre Magazine] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Microsoft contracts 30,000 Rubin GPUs at Nscale's hydro-powered Narvik site
item.description: Stargate Norway's capacity finds a hyperscale offtaker above the Arctic Circle. Cold, cheap, firm power keeps winning the contracts that latency arguments said it could not. [Signal 78, Corroborated, via Data Center Dynamics] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Brazil approves a 5 GW grid connection for Scala's AI City
item.description: Eldorado do Sul's campus gets state sign-off for up to 4.75 GW of planned capacity, roughly $50 billion, with phase one operational. Latin America's largest compute project is now also its most grid-real. [Signal 74, Corroborated, via Data Centre Magazine] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: ByteDance begins construction on a ~$39B campus at Pecém with a 20-year wind PPA
item.description: 300 MW first phase toward roughly 1 GW in Ceará, wind-fired and export-oriented. The largest Chinese AI-infrastructure project abroad is rising in Brazil. [Signal 72, Corroborated, via Data Center Dynamics] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: S&P lifts Paraguay to investment grade, joining Moody's
item.description: BBB- lands on the country holding the index's largest redirectable power surplus relative to size, roughly 40 TWh a year currently exported at commodity prices. Capital access arrives before the compute does. [Signal 84, Confirmed, via Bloomberg] More: https://compute.world/wire.html
